issues.description: Typo 'stlib' in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive should be 'stdlib'.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged the misspelling in the rendered docstring. It lands in published Sphinx output and a deprecation note is part of the API contract, so the typo should be corrected in the same commit.

issues.description: Deprecation message does not show the replacement recipe for the both-streams case.
issues.detail: The warning names contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr but does not explain that callers redirecting both must nest two with-statements (or use ExitStack). Since the deprecated helper accepted both streams in one call, the migration note should give the exact one-line substitution to preserve the original postcondition.

issues.description: New deprecation test exercises stdout only, not the stderr substitution path.
issues.detail: The deprecation message promises substitutability for both redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr, but the test only verifies the stdout path and the warning fires. Adding a stderr case (and ideally the restore-on-exception invariant) would prove the full contract being deprecated rather than a single example.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a clean, contract-preserving deprecation: a bespoke context manager is replaced by stdlib contextlib equivalents that satisfy the same pre/postconditions, with the original generator left untouched under an @deprecated wrapper. Verdict is merge-ready after minor polish. Consensus issues are all P2: a 'stlib' typo in the Sphinx directive, a deprecation message that should hand users the nested-with replacement for the both-streams case, and a test gap on the stderr substitution path. No correctness, substitutability, or design concerns were raised.
